To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have used cDNA microarrays to demonstrate that metastatic colorectal cancer cells have altered expression of genes that may contribute to their invasive properties.

the metastatic colorectal cancer cells exhibit underexpression of genes that regulate cell adhesion and cell signaling, whereas they overexpress genes involved in transcription, translation, and DNA repair.
the metastatic cell SW620 has underexpression of genes that regulate cell adhesion, whereas the nonmetastatic cell SW480 has overexpression of genes that control transcription.

the development and application of microarray-based gene expression analysis in the study of the metastasis of colorectal cancer, a leading cause of cancer mortality in the Western world.

the development of a novel bioinformatics tool to identify chromosomal regions associated with the metastatic progression and the application of this tool to the study of colorectal cancer metastasis.
the molecular mechanisms that underlie the development of metastases in colorectal cancer.
